names.legendary: Bellowsar, Emperor of the Last Waltz

lore.common: Lets out one tiny honk whenever the room goes quiet. It has ruined six marriage proposals.
lore.uncommon: Summons a cheerful polka every time somebody tells a lie. Nobody in its village has dared to fib in years.
lore.rare: One chord from its bellows makes even the grumpiest statues dance. They are furious about it.
lore.epic: Unfurled its bellows across an entire city and played a chord so mighty the bridges began dancing. The mayor requested an encore.
lore.legendary: Inhaled a hurricane through its bellows and exhaled the first song ever written. The winds still hum the chorus, badly.

names.legendary: Maestro Steadfast, Keeper of the Score

lore.common: Holds the music perfectly until somebody leans in to read the difficult bit.
lore.uncommon: Slowly sinks during rehearsal until the violinist must crouch like a frog.
lore.rare: Flips the score to the next page exactly one bar too early. The pianist is now deeply suspicious of breezes.
lore.epic: Threw the entire orchestra's sheet music into the air mid-finale. The players caught random pages and accidentally composed the year's best new symphony.
lore.legendary: Steadfast stood alone through the storm that scattered the great orchestra, guarding the unfinished final score. Decades later the returning musicians found every note still in place.

names.legendary: Maestra Quire, Unwritten Symphony

lore.common: Flips its page when the pianist is still halfway through the first bar.
lore.uncommon: Hides a sharp sign inside a coffee stain, ensuring the trumpeter plays a spectacularly wrong note.
lore.rare: Rearranges its ink into an entirely new song whenever anyone says they are bored of practising.
lore.epic: Escaped the music stands and made a thousand black notes march across the concert hall walls. The audience stood up and sang the wallpaper.
lore.legendary: Maestra Quire holds a symphony no composer has yet imagined. When she opens her paper wings, instruments everywhere play one perfect chord, then spend a century trying to remember it.

names.legendary: Grand Tinelio, Conductor of Brass Dreams

lore.common: Plinks a tiny metal tooth every time its winding key is touched. Sounds alarmingly pleased with itself.
lore.uncommon: Hides a row of metal teeth inside its case and plays them like a microscopic harp.
lore.rare: Changes the rhythm of its pinned cylinder so the same tune becomes a completely new dance.
lore.epic: Its clockwork comb played so loudly that every mechanical clock in the concert hall started joining in. The audience couldn't tell where the orchestra ended.
lore.legendary: Tinelio carved a melody into a cylinder of moonlit brass, then wound it just once. The tune has travelled from music box to music box for three hundred years without losing its final note.

names.legendary: Count Allegro, Lord of the Unbroken Beat

lore.common: Ticks steadily through the piano lesson, judging every note in silence.
lore.uncommon: Stops the moment the music teacher leaves the room, then resumes with an innocent click.
lore.rare: Speeds up whenever the pianist becomes nervous. The pianist has started playing standing up.
lore.epic: Conducted a full orchestra by ticking louder than the brass, sending the violins into a perfectly synchronised tantrum.
lore.legendary: Count Allegro kept the beat of a forgotten symphony after its composer had vanished. Centuries later the music returned, guided by a ticking sound beneath the old theatre.

names.legendary: Tempora, Mistress of the Final Chime

lore.common: Ticks along with the music, then interrupts the quietest passage to announce lunchtime.
lore.uncommon: Rings precisely when the violin solo is about to begin.
lore.rare: Pulls every clock in the rehearsal room into the same rhythm until the walls seem to pulse.
lore.epic: Set the entire marching band to the pace of a town clock, sending them in flawless circles around the park until teatime.
lore.legendary: Tempora once held the final chime of an abandoned clock tower inside her pendulum. When the lost city was found again, every bell rang in perfect time with her heart.

names.legendary: Bongorath, Twin-Heart of the Tides

lore.common: Goes bop-bop whenever someone walks past. It is its own audience.
lore.uncommon: Makes every finger in the room start tapping. The furniture has filed a noise complaint.
lore.rare: Steals the heartbeat of anyone who hears its rhythm for ten seconds. Nobody can walk in a straight line afterward.
lore.epic: Pounded out a rhythm so fierce the sandcastles on the beach marched into the sea in military formation.
lore.legendary: Bongorath learned the first beat from the ocean. When its twin drums speak, the waves obey their tempo and even hurricanes must keep time.

names.legendary: Cajonculus, Heartbeat of the Earth

lore.common: Pretends to be a stool until someone sits down. Then it starts a very personal drum solo.
lore.uncommon: Adds a percussion track to every conversation by rattling beneath the speaker's chair.
lore.rare: Makes every floorboard vibrate in time with its heartbeat. The mice have formed a dance troupe.
lore.epic: Struck one bass note beneath a campfire and woke every sleeping volcano in the district. The sausages danced off their sticks.
lore.legendary: Deep inside Cajonculus beats the rhythm that taught the first forests to sway. It refuses to play encores unless the audience brings cushions.

names.legendary: Congaroth, Heartbeat of the Continent

lore.common: Taps along to your thoughts. This makes lying at dinner very difficult.
lore.uncommon: Demands a dance circle even at funerals. Has been politely disinvited from several.
lore.rare: Its rhythm makes parked cars bounce on their tyres, all perfectly in time.
lore.epic: Played a solo so fierce that every manhole in the city erupted with dancing sewer workers. The mayor declared a holiday.
lore.legendary: Before drums existed, Congaroth taught thunder to keep time. Every storm is merely the sky trying to remember its opening beat.

names.legendary: Djembala, Heartbeat of the Red Earth

lore.common: Slaps its own drumhead when nobody is playing. Claims it is applause.
lore.uncommon: Its ropes tighten themselves whenever someone plays off beat.
lore.rare: Every strike summons footsteps from beneath the floorboards. Nobody has found the dancers.
lore.epic: Called a village-wide rhythm so powerful that the market stalls marched into perfect rows. The mayor had to dance to retrieve his desk.
lore.legendary: The first heartbeat of the savannah is said to echo inside Djembala. When its skin sings, even ancient stones remember how to dance.

names.legendary: Tympanor, Beater of the First Heart

lore.common: Is hit once and booms for five minutes. The drummer calls it enthusiasm.
lore.uncommon: Hides one drumstick before every concert. Claims the other stick is lonely.
lore.rare: Can summon a marching band from the sound of a single beat. The neighbors are considering relocation.
lore.epic: Struck a rhythm so fierce that the entire stadium began marching without moving their feet. The mayor's speech became a drum solo.
lore.legendary: Before the mountains had names, Tympanor struck the heartbeat that woke them. Every thunderstorm is an echo of its next encore.

names.legendary: Tympanor, Heartbeat of the Mountain

lore.common: Waits through ninety minutes of music for one magnificent BONG. Often misses its cue.
lore.uncommon: Changes pitch every time its player presses the pedal and claims the conductor is moving the notes.
lore.rare: Shivers its copper bowl and makes every dessert in the concert hall wobble in time.
lore.epic: Beat a rolling crescendo so mighty that the audience rose three inches from their seats and landed on the downbeat.
lore.legendary: Tympanor was hammered from a fallen bell of the sky and beats once when a mountain awakens. The old orchestra plays softly so it never mistakes a rehearsal for an invitation.

names.legendary: General Ratatam of the Napless Brigade

lore.common: Produces one dull tap, then bangs itself again just to be sure.
lore.uncommon: Rolls away from its drumsticks whenever someone asks for quiet.
lore.rare: Leads an army of stuffed toys around the nursery in perfect marching rhythm.
lore.epic: Played a solo at midnight so loud that every baby monitor in the neighbourhood began conducting the same symphony.
lore.legendary: General Ratatam once marched an army of toy soldiers across a sleeping kingdom without a single soldier losing step. The king woke up furious, then appointed the little drummer royal bandleader.

names.legendary: Gravissimo, Father of the Deepest Note

lore.common: Has to take the bus sideways. Still demands a window seat.
lore.uncommon: Groans when bowed and pretends to be an ancient whale.
lore.rare: One plucked string can shake coins out of a miser's pockets. Jazz clubs employ it discreetly.
lore.epic: Played a bassline so deep that the jazz club sank one floor into the basement. The drummer insisted this improved the acoustics.
lore.legendary: Gravissimo holds the note that first taught the ocean to rumble. Each performance calls an enormous whale to the surface, hoping to meet its long-lost cousin.

names.legendary: Bassilisk, Serpent of the Deep Groove

lore.common: Steals the melody whenever the guitarist looks away.
lore.uncommon: Makes the drummer nod so hard that the cymbals become a blur.
lore.rare: One note can make every speaker in the building crawl toward the stage.
lore.epic: Played a riff so deep that the festival stage began moving like a giant caterpillar. The audience followed it into the neighboring town.
lore.legendary: Bassilisk slumbers beneath the oldest concert hall, curled around a string that hums the pulse of the earth. Every bassist dreams of striking that note once.

names.legendary: Sixstring Sol, the Forbidden Chord

lore.common: Sits in a corner silently judging everyone who says they know three chords.
lore.uncommon: Breaks a string during the best part of a song. Claims the drama improves the performance.
lore.rare: Strums a chord that makes every listener remember a song they have never heard before.
lore.epic: Played one solo so thunderous that all the windows began headbanging. The drummer refused to compete with the weather.
lore.legendary: Sixstring Sol found a seventh chord between its six strings. Every guitar in the land rang in answer; even the oldest forest hummed through its roots.

names.legendary: Sir Lutenhart, Bard of Fallen Towers

lore.common: Has a belly rounder than the minstrel who carries it. Both blame the banquet.
lore.uncommon: Demands so much tuning that the audience ages an entire birthday before the first note.
lore.rare: Makes every listener speak like a medieval knight until midnight. The bus driver now calls everyone 'my liege'.
lore.epic: Played beneath the castle walls until the guards abandoned their posts to join a dance that lasted three nights.
lore.legendary: Sir Lutenhart played one forgotten melody in the ruins of a king's hall. Stone by stone, the hall rebuilt itself to hear the final verse.

names.legendary: Signor Mandorino, Minstrel of the Tides

lore.common: Has twice as many strings as it thinks necessary and complains about tuning them all.
lore.uncommon: Strums so fast that the pigeons begin tapping along on the harbour wall.
lore.rare: Sends little tremors through every glass at the wedding, making the guests toast between verses.
lore.epic: Played beneath the lighthouse until the fishing fleet turned around to hear its final refrain. The catch was forgotten; the fish applauded.
lore.legendary: Signor Mandorino once sang a moonlit serenade that coaxed the sleeping sea into gentle waves. Sailors still hear its eight strings before a safe passage home.

names.legendary: Sitara of the Unending Raga

lore.common: Knocks the lampshade with its long neck whenever somebody picks it up for practice.
lore.uncommon: Hums through its sympathetic strings even when only one note is played.
lore.rare: Bends a note so beautifully that every ribbon, vine and cat's tail in the room bends along.
lore.epic: Played a raga that stretched the evening across three sunsets. The audience stayed for the final note and missed an entire working week.
lore.legendary: Sitara remembers the first melody played under the monsoon stars. Her strings can call back a vanished evening for one last dance, but never rush a single note.

names.legendary: Arphelia, Tamer of the River Song

lore.common: Makes a lovely little plink every time a curious cat brushes past. The cat is learning scales.
lore.uncommon: Needs tuning whenever someone opens a window. The harpist now owns seventeen thermometers.
lore.rare: Can pluck a lullaby from the air without being touched. The audience dreams of places it has never visited.
lore.epic: Played at the royal wedding until every fountain began dancing to the music. The cake joined in and was asked to leave.
lore.legendary: Arphelia persuaded a raging river to flow gently around a sleeping village. Its strings still hum when the spring floods approach.

names.legendary: Magnifico, the Voice Above the Clouds

lore.common: Gets tapped twice and asked 'is this thing on?' every single time.
lore.uncommon: Howls whenever it gets too close to a loudspeaker, then denies responsibility.
lore.rare: Makes the shyest person in the room sound like the confident host of a stadium.
lore.epic: Picked up a whispered joke backstage and broadcast it to the whole theatre. The actors had to wait ten minutes for the laughter to stop.
lore.legendary: Magnifico carried the final song of a distant mountain village across the clouds. On quiet nights, the song returns to the valley as a gentle echo from the stars.

names.legendary: Maestro Grandissimo of the Lost Chord

lore.common: Waits until the room is silent before making one key go PLONK all by itself.
lore.uncommon: Keeps a sticky key in the middle of every tune and calls it artistic interpretation.
lore.rare: Plays the melody of whoever enters the room, including the postman who has never touched a keyboard.
lore.epic: Struck all eighty-eight keys with one thunderous chord. The concert hall shook so hard the chandeliers started conducting.
lore.legendary: Maestro Grandissimo played the lost chord that could end a hundred-year quarrel. For one night even the bells of rival cities rang together in perfect harmony.

names.legendary: Aethermin, Singer of the Untouched

lore.common: Wails whenever somebody reaches past it for a biscuit.
lore.uncommon: Is offended if you touch it. The proper way to say hello is to wave from a distance.
lore.rare: Reads the tiniest motion of a hand and turns it into an eerie melody nobody can sing afterward.
lore.epic: Filled the theatre with an invisible orchestra during the ghost scene. The actors refused to leave their dressing rooms.
lore.legendary: Aethermin played the first song without strings, keys or breath. The spirits drifting between stars still hum its impossible melody when nothing else is moving.

names.legendary: Pianissimo, Emperor of Twelve Notes

lore.common: Plinks the same note twelve times while the adults pretend to enjoy it.
lore.uncommon: Hides one flat note in every tune, even nursery rhymes.
lore.rare: Makes any toddler play a perfect concerto for exactly five minutes, then demands applause and a biscuit.
lore.epic: Challenged the concert hall's grand piano to a duel and won by playing twelve notes so fiercely that the chandeliers hummed along.
lore.legendary: Pianissimo possesses only twelve tiny keys, yet his melody once persuaded a thousand sleeping music boxes to open in unison. Each box revealed a different forgotten lullaby.

names.legendary: Plinkabella, the Rainbow Repairer

lore.common: Plonks its yellow bar whenever the baby finally falls asleep.
lore.uncommon: Steals its little mallet and hides it inside a teddy bear's ear.
lore.rare: Changes each colourful bar into a tiny singing bird when struck with the correct rhythm.
lore.epic: Captain Clattercrash led a nursery marching band across the playground. Their rainbow bars woke the sleeping school bell and made it ring at every wrong hour.
lore.legendary: Plinkabella was given to a child who had never seen a rainbow. She played seven bright notes through the open window, and the sky answered by painting each colour across the rain.

names.legendary: MacHowl, Voice of the Highlands

lore.common: Sounds like a goose trying to reverse out of a trumpet. The goose is suing for defamation.
lore.uncommon: Needs a full minute to inflate before playing. Uses that time to threaten everyone with a solo.
lore.rare: Its three drones can hold one note for nine days. Three villages have filed noise complaints.
lore.epic: Blew a battle hymn across the glens so fiercely that every sheep marched into Edinburgh demanding independence.
lore.legendary: When MacHowl plays, ancient clans answer from the mist. Unfortunately the ghosts know only one song, and it has twelve encores.

names.legendary: Buglorian, Summoner of the First Dawn

lore.common: Can play exactly four notes, all of them loud enough to wake an entire barracks.
lore.uncommon: Sounds the wake-up call on public holidays. Has no understanding of mercy.
lore.rare: Makes anyone who hears it stand to attention, including the ducks and the mayor's lawn gnome.
lore.epic: Called the entire scout camp to breakfast so fiercely that the tents stood up first. The scouts followed in their pyjamas.
lore.legendary: Buglorian blew the first trumpet at the dawn of a forgotten kingdom. Every sleeping soldier woke except the king, who asked for five more minutes and lost the war.

names.legendary: Yidrak, Breath of the Ancient Hollow

lore.common: Hums so deeply the dog thinks a storm has moved into the floorboards.
lore.uncommon: Demands you keep breathing while playing. This feels like a personal attack.
lore.rare: Turns hollow trees into choirs with a single low note. The kookaburras supply commentary.
lore.epic: Sent a rolling drone across the festival grounds that rattled every tent peg loose. The dancers never missed a beat.
lore.legendary: Carved from a sacred hollow tree in an old tale, Yidrak carries voices of wind and earth in a single unbroken breath. Even thunder listens before answering.

names.legendary: Baron Euphonix, the Velvet Thunder

lore.common: Makes a sound like a bear humming itself to sleep inside a brass kettle.
lore.uncommon: Belches one misplaced note whenever the brass band tries to look dignified.
lore.rare: Can soften the grumpiest neighbour with three warm notes. The fourth makes them request an encore.
lore.epic: Played one solo at the village concert and every statue on the green began waltzing. The mayor's statue was asked to leave for stepping on toes.
lore.legendary: Euphonix once soothed a furious mountain with a melody so gentle that its avalanches turned into snowflakes. The mountain now sends him a thank-you card every winter.

names.legendary: Old Bluebreath, Keeper of the Last Train

lore.common: Goes into a pocket perfectly clean and comes out filled with biscuit crumbs.
lore.uncommon: Plays the wrong note when its owner breathes in. Pretends that is an avant-garde solo.
lore.rare: Sings a blues so sad that every milk bottle in the fridge develops a tiny tear.
lore.epic: Played at an empty station until all the trains stopped to listen. The passengers missed their connections and demanded an encore.
lore.legendary: Old Bluebreath learned a tune from a traveller who missed the last train. The melody still guides lonely wanderers home whenever the rails are quiet.

names.legendary: Minimo, the Four-Note Miracle

lore.common: Plays three squeaky notes from the bottom of a pocket. Nobody can find the fourth.
lore.uncommon: Dangles from a keyring and announces every attempt to sneak home quietly.
lore.rare: Creates a melody from a single breath that makes the keys dance across the table.
lore.epic: Fell into a storm drain and turned a whole street into a spontaneous dance floor. The rats formed a brass section.
lore.legendary: Minimo knows only four notes, yet once played them in such perfect order that an entire orchestra stopped rehearsing to listen.

names.legendary: Kazoonius, Herald of the Tiny Orchestra

lore.common: Turns the grandest melody into the sound of an apologetic bee.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to make music unless someone hums directly into its face.
lore.rare: Changes every important speech into a buzzing solo. The head teacher now sends written announcements.
lore.epic: Led a hundred kazoo players through the birthday parade. Every dog in town joined the chorus, and the brass band retired.
lore.legendary: Kazoonius played a tune so ridiculous that even the ancient stone statues laughed. Their smiles remain carved into the town square to this day.

names.legendary: Melodoria, the Breathbound Piano

lore.common: Looks like a toy keyboard until someone starts blowing through its little plastic tube.
lore.uncommon: Collects suspicious puddles in its mouthpiece after every music lesson.
lore.rare: Sends unexpected notes up the nose of anyone who tries to play a masterpiece without breathing.
lore.epic: Played every missing instrument part at the school concert, changing from flute to brass to piano faster than the teacher could turn the pages.
lore.legendary: Melodoria learned her first melody from the wind itself. On a still night, her keys can summon an entire invisible orchestra to play for those who cannot sleep.

names.legendary: Piccolina, Voice Above the Storm

lore.common: Makes a sound so high that the dog leaves the room before practice begins.
lore.uncommon: Sneaks one shrill note above every flute solo and smiles innocently.
lore.rare: Calls bats from the church tower with a single note. They arrive with strongly worded complaints.
lore.epic: Outplayed an entire marching band from the far end of the parade. A thousand windows chimed along in protest.
lore.legendary: Piccolina played one pure note across the mountain pass during a snowstorm. The stranded travellers followed it to safety while the blizzard tried and failed to sing louder.

names.legendary: Recordora, Piper of the First Dawn

lore.common: Produces one heroic squeak when the student meant to play a gentle note.
lore.uncommon: Plays a nursery rhyme again and again until the family starts humming in its sleep.
lore.rare: Plays a note so high that every dog in the village sits up to listen.
lore.epic: Led the school orchestra in a concert so piercing that every window in the hall began singing along.
lore.legendary: Recordora played one note so pure that every bird in the royal aviary began harmonising. The school music teacher still refuses to believe it was a recorder.

names.legendary: Grand Oompharius, the Walking Cathedral

lore.common: Wears its own brass body like a coiled snake and bonks every doorway on parade day.
lore.uncommon: Uses its giant bell as a rain catcher. The bandleader has started bringing a bucket.
lore.rare: Blasts one enormous note that turns marching feet into perfectly synchronised dancers.
lore.epic: Marched through the capital with a note so deep that the statues rose from their pedestals and joined the procession.
lore.legendary: Oompharius carried the sound of a forgotten city's last festival inside his bell for centuries. When he finally played it, the empty streets filled with dancing shadows.

names.legendary: Trumpetorius, Herald of the Morning Star

lore.common: Practises the loudest note it knows during the neighbour's afternoon nap.
lore.uncommon: Jams one valve whenever its player tries to impress someone.
lore.rare: Blows a heroic fanfare and makes every pigeon in the square form an honour guard.
lore.epic: Sounded one triumphant note over the city and woke every sleeping statue, which immediately demanded marching-band uniforms.
lore.legendary: Trumpetorius sounded the first fanfare when the sun rose over a nameless kingdom. His golden bell still summons courage in frightened hearts, although he insists everyone stand for the difficult high notes.

names.legendary: Stradivara, the Soul of the Strings

lore.common: Squawks when its bow slips, then blames the musician's chin.
lore.uncommon: Teaches the neighbourhood cats a deeply unpleasant new note.
lore.rare: Can make even a stone gargoyle cry with one trembling melody.
lore.epic: Played a solo so fierce that every clock stopped to listen. The concert ran three hours late, and not one person complained.
lore.legendary: Was carved from a tree that grew beside an ancient battlefield. Its strings can remember any melody ever played for peace, including those sung by people long forgotten.

names.legendary: General Bananaparte, Lord of the Bunch

lore.common: Always insists on travelling with its six closest relatives. All six are equally needy.
lore.uncommon: Ripens as a group, preferably the day after you buy them. They call it solidarity.
lore.rare: Every banana in the bunch screams when one is peeled. Nobody has enjoyed a quiet smoothie since.
lore.epic: Marched its yellow army through the supermarket and seized the fruit aisle. The oranges formed a resistance.
lore.legendary: Commands an endless battalion of bananas. Every time one soldier falls, two more appear, and the enemy slips on both of them.

names.legendary: Lord Slipstream, Patron of Bad Timing

lore.common: Waits on the kitchen floor with the patience of a cartoon villain.
lore.uncommon: Can look completely harmless until someone carries a full tray of drinks.
lore.rare: Turns one careless step into a flawless triple pirouette. The ballet school has complained.
lore.epic: Sent an entire football team sliding into the dugout while their coach was explaining the importance of balance.
lore.legendary: An ancient curse disguised as fruit waste. Every famous pratfall in history has been its audition, and not one has met its standards.

names.legendary: Countess Neapolita, Queen of Scoops

lore.common: Refuses to share its cherry, even with the person who ordered it.
lore.uncommon: Melts slowly while everyone argues about who gets the chocolate sauce. Enjoys the tension.
lore.rare: Can clone its ice-cream scoops, but only when nobody brought enough spoons.
lore.epic: Rolled a banana split the length of the promenade. The tourists thought it was a new coastal railway.
lore.legendary: Her three enchanted scoops can freeze a heatwave, summon a chocolate monsoon and make the gods fight over the last cherry.

names.legendary: Veritoll, the Bell That Cannot Lie

lore.common: Rings whenever anyone sneezes nearby. Thinks it is offering encouragement.
lore.uncommon: Has a voice three sizes larger than its body. Never learned to whisper.
lore.rare: Sounds a tiny DING each time somebody tells a lie. Birthday surprises have become extremely difficult.
lore.epic: Rang so fiercely at lunchtime that every clock tower answered and the entire city arrived for dinner.
lore.legendary: In the oldest tower hangs Veritoll, whose single note forces every ruler to speak the truth. Kings have been trying to steal its clapper for centuries.

names.legendary: Castanara, Dancer of the Lightning Hands

lore.common: Clacks exactly once during the quietest moment of a performance. The conductor knows who did it.
lore.uncommon: Gets stuck to the drummer's fingers and refuses to observe any tempo but its own.
lore.rare: Clicks so quickly that everyone's teeth chatter in sympathy. Dentists love its recitals.
lore.epic: Commanded a thousand dancers with one furious rhythm. The ballroom floor began tapping back, and the chandeliers begged for a slower number.
lore.legendary: Castanara taught lightning how to strike in time to music. When she dances beneath a storm, the thunder follows her heels like an obedient orchestra.

names.legendary: Tollarius, Voice of the Seven Valleys

lore.common: Rings one minute early every Sunday. The bakery has stopped trusting clocks.
lore.uncommon: Wakes the entire village except the one person who asked for the alarm.
lore.rare: Rings a warning five minutes before any disaster within seven hills. Farmers adore it; surprise parties have become impossible.
lore.epic: Rang a single peal that shook the stones from the castle's ancient walls. The council classified it as a very enthusiastic reminder of service times.
lore.legendary: Tollarius carries the last echo of a kingdom drowned beneath a lake. Once each century he rings, and every lost bell under the water answers.

names.legendary: Belladonna, Voice of the Seven Herds

lore.common: Rings whenever its cow is up to something it shouldn't be. So, constantly.
lore.uncommon: Clangs at such awkward times the farmer thinks it knows swear words.
lore.rare: Summons cattle from miles away, even when attached to a confused bicycle.
lore.epic: Its mountain-sized clang brought every cow in the Alps to one meadow. Nobody could find the meadow afterward.
lore.legendary: Was cast from the first star to fall on a pasture. One solemn note can call a wandering herd home from any distance, including a very distant moon.

names.legendary: Zildragor, Herald of the Final Crash

lore.common: Waits forty minutes for its one dramatic moment, then misses it.
lore.uncommon: Keeps shimmering long after the song is over. Audience members blame the violinists.
lore.rare: Can shatter a tense silence without touching a single glass.
lore.epic: Crashed during a royal speech and knocked every crown sideways in the kingdom. The orchestra denied involvement.
lore.legendary: Forged where lightning struck the first ocean, Zildragor's crash can divide storm clouds like curtains. Every thunderclap since has been a poor imitation.

names.legendary: Plectra, Thief of the Final Solo

lore.common: Slips between the sofa cushions as soon as the first chord sounds. It likes the acoustics down there.
lore.uncommon: Hides in a guitarist's shoe for a whole rehearsal. Insists it's part of the rhythm section.
lore.rare: Skips over strings without being touched, playing a solo that makes the guitarist deeply suspicious.
lore.epic: Vanished during the festival's final song and reappeared inside every musician's pocket at once. Nobody has admitted which solo was theirs.
lore.legendary: Plectra was forged from the last note of a forgotten masterpiece. It chooses a different guitarist each century and teaches them a song no one can remember afterwards.

names.legendary: Belladonna, Voice of the Silent Tower

lore.common: Rings whenever the teacher turns to write on the board and looks innocent when they turn back.
lore.uncommon: Sings one clear note during a quiet moment, then refuses to repeat it for witnesses.
lore.rare: Rings whenever someone nearby is daydreaming. The entire classroom has become a symphony.
lore.epic: Gathered every handbell from the village choir into one ringing storm. The bells rehearsed for three days without musicians.
lore.legendary: Belladonna rang once from a bell tower that had stood silent for a thousand years. Every missing traveller heard the note and found the road home.

names.legendary: Tssarion, Keeper of the Unbroken Beat

lore.common: Snaps its cymbals together whenever somebody is about to say something important.
lore.uncommon: Hisses for precisely one beat too long and makes the drummer blame the microphone.
lore.rare: Can keep a band in time even when its members are playing four completely different songs.
lore.epic: Started a rhythm at the jazz festival that made every foot in the audience tap together. The pavement applied for sick leave.
lore.legendary: Tssarion has kept the heartbeat of an ancient city steady since the last musician vanished. On quiet nights the street lamps still flicker in time with its silver cymbals.

names.legendary: Plantarion, Keeper of the Golden Slice

lore.common: Crunches loudly enough that everybody knows who raided the snack cupboard.
lore.uncommon: Snaps in half when dipped, then blames the salsa for being too aggressive.
lore.rare: Spins through the air like a tiny golden disc, landing neatly in the one bowl nobody ordered.
lore.epic: Shook the stadium with one monstrous crunch, scattering crisp fragments over every seat. The seagulls bought season tickets.
lore.legendary: Plantarion once fed a lost island crew with a single sack of golden plantain slices. Each morning the sack was full again, but only if the sailors shared with the seabirds.

names.legendary: Rainshara, Voice of the Sleeping Clouds

lore.common: Makes the sound of a small shower and tricks everyone into closing the windows.
lore.uncommon: Rattles its hidden seeds so soothingly that the dog falls asleep standing up.
lore.rare: Imitates a storm so perfectly that frogs crawl out of their ponds to listen.
lore.epic: Led an orchestra of rain sticks across the dry fields. Its final note summoned a cloud shaped like a standing ovation.
lore.legendary: Rainshara shook a desert's drought loose with one slow turn. The first rain fell so heavily that the camels held an emergency umbrella meeting.

names.legendary: Maracondo, Carnival Heartbeat

lore.common: Rattles inside the toy basket whenever someone whispers that the baby is asleep.
lore.uncommon: Steals one bead from its neighbour and immediately sounds out of tune.
lore.rare: Starts the correct percussion beat for any song, including the one everyone is embarrassed to know.
lore.epic: Shook so furiously at carnival that every loose object in the city joined the rhythm. Parking meters danced better than the mayor.
lore.legendary: Maracondo carries the first beat of every festival in a hollow gourd. Strike it once and distant dancers remember each other across oceans, regardless of where they learned the steps.

names.legendary: Aumara, the Bronze Breath of Stillness

lore.common: Hums when somebody brushes its rim, making the family cat look for the invisible bee.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to vibrate until the person holding it stops checking their phone.
lore.rare: Sends one warm note rolling through the room, calming even the kettle that has been boiling in a temper.
lore.epic: Rang so deeply during a crowded festival that everyone stopped arguing at once. The musicians stood confused in the silence, then bowed.
lore.legendary: Aumara holds a note struck before the oldest mountain learned its name. Listen closely and the sound stretches one peaceful moment across a thousand restless lifetimes.

names.legendary: Trigonella, the Last Note of Creation

lore.common: Waits through a whole symphony for one ting and drops its little metal striker.
lore.uncommon: Chimes every time someone says the concert has finished.
lore.rare: Strikes a note so pure that every piece of cutlery in the theatre rings back.
lore.epic: Sounded a single glittering note over a noisy orchestra and silenced a thousand instruments, including an especially offended tuba.
lore.legendary: Trigonella was forged from three slivers of the first bell and can hear every missing note in the world. She rings only when a forgotten melody is ready to return.

names.legendary: Aeoloria, the Wind's Forgotten Song

lore.common: Tinkles at the smallest breeze and demands everyone admire the tune.
lore.uncommon: Jangles all night while the neighbours wish it would learn a lullaby.
lore.rare: Hears storms approaching and plays their opening notes hours in advance.
lore.epic: Conducted a summer gale with a thousand silver chimes. Every house in the street rang in a different key, and the thunder kept losing its place.
lore.legendary: Once taught the wind a melody that calmed the great sea. Even now, sailors know that when its ancient bells sing, the waves will soon lie still.

names.legendary: Xylarion, the Staircase of Notes

lore.common: Gets its wooden bars played in the wrong order by an ambitious toddler.
lore.uncommon: Hides its mallets, then complains that nobody appreciates live music.
lore.rare: Strikes notes so clear that glass flowers bloom along the audience's windowsill.
lore.epic: Maestro Thunderbars turned a grand concert into a bouncing wooden dance floor. Each note sent the orchestra leaping to a different balcony.
lore.legendary: Xylarion built a staircase from seven notes that only appears when played in the correct order. One curious child climbed the melody and found a cloud rehearsing thunder with a pair of mallets.
